principles: No-experiment mode is byte-identical to today at every entrypoint (experiment is strictly opt-in)
One shared leaf for the arm decision — no per-handler arm logic
Gate only the render; compute and log on both arms (control is the instrumented shadow)
Mechanical enforcement over instructions: blocking in the CLI engine, violations as structured events
The arm never touches gate decisions, blockers, or prompt hashes
drivers: M6/M7 arm-runs execute lattice commands in isolated workspaces via a campaign runner that can set per-process environment
Plan section 9 requires recorded retrieval violations countable by the M4 scorer (retrievalViolationCount)
Seven render sites with two render shapes (full renderMemoryFreshnessPack and renderMemoryFreshnessPackSummary in done-prepare)
B-5a48 precedent: shared firing leaf eliminated per-site drift for hints

options.name: env-var-context
pros: Per-process scoping matches the campaign runner model (each arm-run is a separate process tree)
Zero persistent repo state — a crashed run cannot leave experiment mode active
cons: A stray exported env var could suppress pack rendering (mitigated: require BOTH vars, validate arm value, stamp events with experimentId)

options.name: arm-context-file
pros: Survives across processes without env plumbing
cons: Repo state leaks between runs — a crashed run silently poisons subsequent commands
Cannot express per-process arm identity when both arms share one machine
Cleanup discipline becomes a new failure mode

options.name: per-command-flag
cons: A missed flag silently mixes arms mid-task
Does not cover implicit internal renders

rationale: The env-var context (LATTICE_EXPERIMENT_ID + LATTICE_EXPERIMENT_ARM, both required, validated) matches the process-per-arm-run execution model of the M6/M7 campaign runner, keeps zero persistent repo state so a crashed run cannot leak experiment mode into production, and makes per-run arm identity structurally constant for the whole process tree. Stray-env risk is mitigated by refusing partial context, validating the arm value, warning on partial context, and stamping every surfaced/violation event with the active experimentId. The resolved-learning-root inspection surface goes on observability_snapshot (existing read-only JSON command) — smallest new surface.

preMortem.scenario: A developer shell has LATTICE_EXPERIMENT_ARM=control exported from an earlier debugging session; weeks later normal lattice commands silently stop rendering the memory pack and block recall
preMortem.consequence: Sessions lose memory advisories and retrieval; activity log polluted with violations
preMortem.mitigation: resolveExperimentArm requires BOTH vars and a valid arm value else null; exactly-one-set prints a warning naming the ignored var; block messages name the experimentId; smoke covers partial-context

preMortem.scenario: One of the seven handler sites (e.g. done-prepare summary path) bypasses the shared leaf so control-arm runs still render the pack there
preMortem.trigger: The full vs summary render shapes diverge during wiring
preMortem.consequence: Control arm contaminated at one entrypoint — paired comparison biased; M7 campaign invalidated (plan 11.3 stopping-rule breach)
preMortem.mitigation: Smoke asserts NO pack section at ALL seven entrypoints on control (grep full command output); M6 pilot re-audits per plan

preMortem.scenario: The retrieval block list drifts from the command catalog — a later memory-consuming command is not blocked on control
preMortem.trigger: Hand-maintained block array separate from the catalog
preMortem.consequence: Control arm can retrieve memory via the unblocked command; isolation silently broken
preMortem.mitigation: Block classification co-located with catalog entries (ownershipClass pattern); smoke cross-checks every command matching the memory families (recall, dev_memory_*, playbook_*, learning_*, memory_playbook_baseline_*) carries the marker

preMortem.scenario: The arm leaks into resolveReviewPromptHash or reviewer runId binding via the rendered section, breaking review-run signatures repo-wide after merge
preMortem.trigger: A handler concatenates the gated section into a hashed prompt domain
preMortem.consequence: Reviewer evidence reads stale/tampered for every active story
preMortem.mitigation: Smoke asserts resolveReviewPromptHash byte-identical across arms (extends existing ab-shadow-gate invariance case); review checklist verifies no hash-domain consumer

preMortem.scenario: experience_pack_surfaced fires on every command, bloating activity.jsonl and slowing readActivityLogTail consumers during campaigns
preMortem.trigger: No dedup on the new event
preMortem.consequence: Unbounded log growth; all lifecycle commands slow down
preMortem.mitigation: Dedup keyed on (experimentId, consumer, storyId/roundKey) per plan.md; M6 pilot checks per-run log growth
